summary: Heiner Eichner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1964–1974). He later held a post at the University of Vienna (~1989–2010).
Heinrich August Eduard Schaeffer was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig. He served as principal at the Evangelical Lutheran Central High School.

Heinrich August Jäschke was a Tibetologist and linguist. Educated at Pädagogium Niesky (~1831–1837) and Gnadenfeld Theological Seminary (~1837–1839), he taught at Christiansfeld (1837–1842), served as co-director at Niesky (1842–1856), and was a Moravian missionary in Kyelang (1856–1863) and the Moravian Church (1857–1868).

Heinrich Blatt was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the universities of Munich, Leipzig, Berlin, Würzburg, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (Ph.D. ~1922–1923). He worked as a librarian at Würzburg University Library from 1923 to 1946.

Heinrich Blochmann was an Indologist and historian. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer at Leipzig (1855), Karl Benedikt Hase at Paris (1857), and at Calcutta. He served at Aliah University (Assistant Professor 1860; Principal 1865, 1870) and was Secretary of The Asiatic Society (1868–1878).
Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Bonn (~1839–1843). He held a post at the University of Munich from around 1865 to 1894.

Heinrich Düntzer was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker at the University of Bonn (1830–1837) and under Franz Bopp in Berlin (1835). He held posts at Bonn (~1836–1846) and as librarian at Dreikönigsgymnasium (1846–1885).

Heinrich Ewald was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Thomas Christian Tychsen at the University of Göttingen (1820–1823), where he later served as professor (1824–1837, 1848–1867), and held a post at the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

Heinrich Franz Joseph Junker was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Giessen, Strasbourg, and Heidelberg under Christian Bartholomae (Ph.D. ~1910–1911), later holding professorships at Hamburg (1919, 1923), Leipzig (1926–1945), and Humboldt University (1951).
Heinrich Gustav Hotho was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1820–1826) and subsequently held a post there from around 1829 to 1873.
Heinrich Gössel was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1908–1913, Ph.D.). He served as an assistant at the University of Leipzig in 1917.

Heinrich Hackmann worked in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Basel, served as Privatdozent at Göttingen (~1890–1894), and was ordinary professor of the history of religions at the University of Amsterdam (1913–1934).

Heinrich Hettrich was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Giessen, Saarland, and Munich. He taught at Saarland, Munich, and Marburg, before holding the chair for comparative linguistics at the University of Würzburg starting in 1989.

Heinrich Hübschmann was a linguist and specialist in Iranian and Indology. He studied at Jena under August Schleicher (1868), Tübingen, Munich under Martin Haug, and Leipzig, later serving as professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Strasbourg from 1877.

Heinrich Kiepert was a geographer and historian who studied at Berlin under August Boeckh, Leopold von Ranke, and Julius Heinrich Petermann, and at Jena. He directed cartographic offices in Weimar and Berlin and became ordinary professor of geography at Berlin in 1874.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was an Orientalist and linguist. He studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig (1819–1824) and under Silvestre de Sacy, Caussin de Perceval, Chézy, and Jaubert in Paris, later holding the chair for Oriental languages at Leipzig from 1836.

Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn at the University of Göttingen. He served as chair of Ancient Indian Language and Literature at Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1935) and secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1920–1938).

Heinrich Meinhard was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn under Willibald Kirfel (~1923–1928). He held posts at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (~1929–1937), Pitt Rivers Museum (1938–1947), and Durham University (1950).

Heinrich Meyer-Benfey was an Indology and German scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1888–1893). He later served at the University of Hamburg as Privatdozent (1919) and associate professor of German (1923–1938).

Heinrich Nau was an Indologist who studied at the University of Marburg, Concordia Seminary (~1901–1905), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1918–1920), where he earned his Ph.D. under Eugen Hultzsch.
